newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army Aberdeen base commander to retire.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army Aberdeen base commander to retire.

text.p: The commander of the U.S. Army's scandal-plagued Aberdeen Proving Ground, Gen. John Longhouser, is to retire from the military effective June 30, a base spokesman said Tuesday.

"He is retiring," base spokesman John Yaquiant said. He said it was not clear whether Longhouser, who did not have formal authority over the base's Ordnance Center and School where 12 trainers were charged in a major sexual misconduct scandal, may issue a statement regarding his retirement.

Longhouser, 53, is a 32-year Army veteran. He took command of the Aberdeen base in September 1996, serving dual roles as the base's commander and the commander of the U.S. Army's Test and Evaluation Command, which tests proposed weapons at Aberdeen and other bases.

Yaquiant said Longhouser did not have direct disciplinary responsibilty for the base's Ordnance Center and School, which is part of the Army's Training and Doctrine Command, a separate unit from the Test and Evaluation Command.

Maj. Gen. George Friel, commander of the Army's Chemical and Biological Defense Command, has assumed as of Tuesday temporary command of the the proving ground and Test and Evaluation Command, Yaquiant said.

Of the 12 Ordnance Center and School trainers charged in a sexual misconduct investigation that was disclosed in November 1996, four soldiers were found guilty of violations, two received discharges in lieu of court martial, and six are still awaiting resolution of their cases.
